unmapped_findings: For the 19Al alloy the optimal aging temperature range to achieve ultra-high (>900 HV) hardness was mainly 575–625 °C, shifted upward relative to 15Al and 17Al, reflecting the slowed β-Mn precipitation kinetics with increasing Al content.
At temperatures of 600 °C and above, the α matrix of the 19Al alloy had almost completely transformed into β-Mn within just 1 h of aging, with numerous fine BCC and FCC precipitates within the β-Mn.
The 19Al alloy has the highest Al content of the studied series (19Al, Fe 41.6 / Mn 34.8 / Al 18.6 / Cu 5.0 at.%) and its solution-treated state is single-phase α (BCC).

Hardness of the 19Al alloy at 625 °C increased only slightly with aging time (855.6 ± 20.8 HV at 1 h, 863.9 ± 15.8 HV at 3 h, 870.7 ± 16.1 HV at 6 h, 869.5 ± 8.6 HV at 10 h), i.e. the 625 °C hardness is essentially time-independent.
